pages.text: Before you can produce the next evolution of machines, you need to craft $(item)Advanced PCBs$(). Which is a form of advanced computation circuit that is much better at calculations than your previous designs.$(br2)Craft $(item)Empty PCBs$() in the $(item)Pressure Chamber$() then prepare those for etching in a $(item)UV Light Box$(). We can trade you schematics for the light box through the $(item)Amadron Tablet$().

The $(item)UV Light Box$() is powered by pressure and can be sped up by $(item)Speed Upgrades$().$(br2)The $(item)UV Light Box$() exposes the circuit to powerful UV Light, making the etch success chance go up.

pages.title: Circuit Etching
pages.description1: Drop the $(item)Empty PCBs$() in $(item)Etching Acid$() to finish the etching process.$(br2)This process may take a few minutes. We recommend doing a stack or so at a time, to alleviate this chore.

pages.text: Once the etching process is complete, you can craft the $(item)Printed Circuit Board$() with $(item)Capacitors$() and $(item)Transistors$()$(br2)The final step is to create $(item)Advanced PCBs$() in the $(item)Industrial Assembler$().

Once you have some circuit boards made, its probably a wise decision to invest in some upgraded tech that lets you create the $(item)Unassembled PCBs$() easier.$(br2)Enter, the $(item)Assembly Controller$().

pages.title: Assembly Controller
pages.text: The Assembly Controller can take $(item)Empty PCBs$() straight from the $(item)Pressure Chamber$() and turn them into $(item)Unassembled PCBs$() without the PCBs ever being exposed in the $(item)UV Light Box$(), or being submerged in $(item)Etching Acid$().$(br2)It can also make the advanced components that can withstand 20 bars of pressure. More info can be found in the $(item)PNC:R Manual$() under $(item)Manufacturing/Assembly System$().
